front: What is a combinational logic gate?
back: Gates built from multiple basic logic gates. For example NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR etc.
A circuit that takes n input lines and activates one of 2ⁿ output lines based on the input combination.
The concept of choosing between multiple input options. In reality is normally just a MUX.
Multiplexors take a number of data inputs and some select lines and output a single output given the select lines.

front: Which gates make up a half adder?
Which gates make up a full adder?
back:
A AND and XOR gate to add the previous carry and A. (SUM)
A AND and XOR gate to add A and B.
An OR gate to combine the output of each AND gate.
The time required to transfer a message between source and destination.

front: What are the 4 main types of latency delays?
back: Transmission delay — the time it takes to push all the bits of the message onto the wire Propagation delay — the time it takes for the signal to physically travel from source to destination through the medium Processing delay — the time routers/switches take to examine and process the packet Routing delay — the time a packet spends waiting in a buffer/queue at a router before being processed

front: What are the 4 main network topologies?
back: Star (central node, all other nodes connect directly to it) Bus (single wire with multiple connections) Ring (circle wire with nodes along the way, travels in one direction) Mesh (grid of wires)
Instead of passing communication from computer to computer directly, you go computer → switch → computer. There may be multiple switches in between.
